findings.issue: The general rule for building a root-position triad (start on the root, add the third above, add the fifth above, all within the key) and the concept of 'root position' were already taught in L1#10 'Tonic Triads & Scale Degrees'. This block re-explains the rule from scratch rather than briefly recapping it.
findings.evidence: 'The rule for building any root-position triad: 1. Start on your chosen scale degree (the root). 2. Add the note that is a third above it in the scale. 3. Add the note that is a fifth above the root in the scale.'
findings.fix: Compress to a one-line recap, e.g. 'As you learned earlier, a root-position triad stacks a third and a fifth above the root; here we simply start on degree 4 instead of 1.'

findings.issue: Repetitive vague phrasing ('You will find that...' twice) reads as motivational padding rather than instruction.
findings.evidence: "You will find that once you know the scale very well... You will find that the tonic (chord I) feels like home... the subdominant (chord IV) feels like we are travelling a little..."
findings.fix: Tighten to one sentence, e.g. state the shortcut once and describe the functions plainly without the doubled 'You will find that'.
